claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast high-entropy alloy with high configurational disorder.
The superconducting behavior of the starting alloy is uncharacterized.
High configurational disorder homogenizes the electronic environment.
Homogenization of the electronic environment suppresses anisotropic superconducting properties.
A highly disordered alloy will have lower superconducting effective-mass anisotropy than a structurally more ordered control.
High configurational entropy produces a homogeneous distribution of atomic-scale scattering centers.
The distribution of scattering centers averages out directional disparities in electron pairing and effective mass.
Random atomic arrangement enhances electron scattering.
Enhanced scattering reduces directional variation of the superconducting-electron effective mass.
Suppressed electronic anisotropy favors an isotropic superconducting pairing state.
Angular-dependent resistivity under different magnetic-field orientations can be analyzed with an effective-mass scaling model to estimate the superconducting anisotropy parameter gamma_s.
The disordered alloy will show significantly less angular variation in resistivity than the reduced-disorder control.
The disordered alloy will have a lower gamma_s than the reduced-disorder control.
Post-casting annealing can produce a control with reduced configurational disorder.
A reduced-disorder control exhibits greater superconducting anisotropy in angular-dependent resistivity.
The proposed disorder-dependent anisotropy difference should be observable well below Tc under moderate magnetic fields.
Near Tc or at fields sufficiently high to suppress superconductivity, the anisotropy difference may become indiscernible.
Angular-dependent resistivity has been successfully used to determine superconducting anisotropy in another superconducting material.
The quantitative effect of extreme configurational disorder on gamma_s may depend on sample preparation and measurement resolution.
The hypothesis is falsified if the disordered samples have gamma_s values statistically similar to or greater than those of the ordered controls.

contradictions.description: The superconducting behavior and Tc are said to be uncharacterized, but the protocol presupposes that the alloy can be cooled into a superconducting regime and held well below Tc without specifying an initial Tc-discovery step.

The baseline allows either annealing or use of lower-mixing-entropy components; the latter changes composition and is not the same controlled comparison as the annealed, nominally composition-matched control specified in the falsification design.
